solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Support expert recording about loud ringleader

parts.note: a pro is an expert

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the recording wraps round the loud letter

parts.note: a video is a recording
F is forte, the musical abbreviation for loud
the leading letter of 'ring' is R

explanation.surface: Backing a professional recording that features a noisy gang boss.
explanation.definitionFit: To provide for someone is to support them financially, a common phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Starts to photograph in extremely dated black and white

indicators.note: starts of the following words means taking the opening letter of each one

explanation.surface: Starting to take pictures in very old-fashioned monochrome film.
explanation.definitionFit: Pied describes animals or birds patched in two colours, typically black and white, like a magpie.

clue.text: Actor put his heart into musical

indicators.note: put into means one piece is placed inside the other, the musical taking in the heart

parts.note: Oliver! is the Lionel Bart musical

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter, here of 'his'

explanation.surface: A performer threw himself wholeheartedly into a stage musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Olivier was the celebrated English stage and screen actor, who also filmed this puzzle's Shakespeare play.

clue.text: Holding pipe, I chew; missing a little bit of baccy is never-ending

indicators.note: holding means the outer letters keep the pipe inside them
missing means the named letter is dropped from the word for chew

parts.note: to nibble is to chew a little

indicators.note: a little bit of a word is its first letter, here of 'baccy'

parts.note: an exhaust is a pipe on a car

explanation.surface: A pipe smoker chewing on his stem, short of tobacco, rambles on endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pipe' suggests a smoker's briar, but it is a car's exhaust pipe; 'missing' drops B, the first of 'baccy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inexhaustible can never be used up, so it is effectively endless.

clue.text: One of audience heard one leaving city

indicators.note: heard means the solver goes by how the phrase is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: someone leaving is an exiter

explanation.surface: A spectator heard someone walking out of town.
explanation.walkthrough: The unstated theme is Shakespeare's Henry V: 'One of audience' means one of those hearing King Henry's 'Once more unto the breach' speech, here the Duke of Exeter.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeter is the county city of Devon, and the Duke of Exeter is Henry's uncle in the play.

clue.text: "I scorn death before armed encounter with last of French formation"

definitions.text: "I scorn death before armed encounter with last of French formation"

indicators.note: formation means the letters are formed into a new arrangement

parts.words: I scorn death before armed encounter

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, here of 'French'

explanation.surface: A soldier's defiant cry before battle with the French.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of the first six words plus H makes the opening of King Henry's speech before Harfleur in Shakespeare's Henry V.
explanation.definitionFit: The rallying cry urges troops back into battle with scorn for death, so the whole clue describes the quotation.

clue.text: Beam at herb tea taster finishes

indicators.note: finishes of the words means taking the final letter of each

explanation.surface: Someone smiles at a sip of herbal tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beam' looks like a smile, but here it is the structural girder.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-bar is a metal beam with a T-shaped cross-section, used in construction.

clue.text: One of audience slightly snubbed for drinking in town

indicators.note: in means the letters lie inside the run of words 'snubbed for drinking'

explanation.surface: A spectator was given the cold shoulder for boozing in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slightly' tells you only part of 'snubbed for drinking' is wanted. The Duke of Bedford is Henry's brother in Henry V, one of those listening to his speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedford is the county town of Bedfordshire, north of London, and the Duke of Bedford is a character in the play.

clue.text: Riotous bible studies for a band

parts.note: RI is religious instruction, the old British school subject
pro means for, in favour of
a ring is a band

explanation.surface: Scripture classes held for a pop group got wild.
explanation.walkthrough: RI, religious instruction, was a school subject in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A rip-roaring party is boisterous and wild, which is what riotous describes.

clue.text: Curse second degree awful solvers

indicators.note: second means the second letter of the word 'degree'

parts.note: vile means awful
ye is an old word for you, the solvers being addressed

explanation.surface: An academic swears at the readers over a poor second-class degree.
explanation.definitionFit: The evil eye is a malevolent look believed to cast a curse or bring misfortune.

clue.text: Downs aren't sharp

definitions.meaning: in a crossword, down clues run downwards, so they are not set going up
sharp here means well-informed and alert

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition reads the answer as 'clued up(wards)', which down entries in a grid are not.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone clued-up is well informed, knowing and on the ball.

clue.text: See 5
Crown protection for colonists

parts.note: the crown is the top of the head, and colonial officials in hot countries shielded it with a cork-lined hat, not royal favour

explanation.walkthrough: 'Crown' suggests royal protection of a colony; it is the top of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Lightweight sun hats of cork or pith were standard headgear for Europeans in tropical colonies.

clue.text: Artist took heart about first night

indicators.note: about means going round, the heart of the word wrapping the next letter
the heart of a word is its middle letters, here of 'took'
first of a word is its opening letter, here of 'night'

explanation.surface: A painter plucked up courage before an opening night.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoko Ono is a Japanese-born conceptual artist and musician.

clue.text: One of audience reported most of big loss to City

indicators.note: most of a three-letter word drops its first two letters, leaving only the last
reported means the words are taken as spoken, not as written

parts.note: the phrase said aloud, with an unstressed 'to', matches the ending of the city's name

explanation.surface: A spectator heard of a large deficit for the financial City.
explanation.walkthrough: The city's name is said 'Gloster', so G plus 'loss to' said casually gives its sound. The Duke of Gloucester is Henry's brother in Henry V.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloucester is the county city of Gloucestershire in western England, and the Duke of Gloucester appears in the play.

clue.text: The French bishop ready and willing for whip

parts.note: la is the French feminine for the
RR is Right Reverend, the title of a bishop
up for it means ready and willing

explanation.surface: A French cleric eager to use the lash.
explanation.walkthrough: A bishop is styled the Right Reverend, abbreviated RR.
explanation.definitionFit: To larrup is an informal, chiefly dialect verb meaning to thrash or beat soundly.

clue.text: Richard III was tormented, corrupted, beheaded

indicators.note: tormented means the letters are twisted into a new order
beheaded means the word loses its first letter

explanation.surface: The hunchback king was tortured and depraved, then executed.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the head of 'corrupted' leaves ORRUPTED, which 'tormented' rearranges. 'Richard III was' wants a description of his character; it means his place in history.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard III was the last Plantagenet king, reigning before the Tudors took the throne in 1485.

clue.text: Cereal's eaten — finally prepared to face cream, maybe

indicators.note: prepared means the letters are made up into a new form

parts.note: the word is used letter for letter, its S included

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of 'eaten'

explanation.surface: Breakfast cereal has been eaten and someone finally gets ready to put on face cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleanser is a cosmetic lotion for the face, of which face cream is one kind.

clue.text: Trouble undoing steel nut

indicators.note: undoing means the letters are taken apart and put back in another order

explanation.surface: A mechanic struggles to loosen a seized steel nut.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsettle someone is to disturb or trouble them, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Locks care home endless OAPs trashed

indicators.note: trashed means the letters are wrecked into a new order
endless means the last letter of 'home' is dropped

explanation.surface: A care home has its doors locked forever after the residents wreck it.
explanation.walkthrough: OAPs are old-age pensioners, British for senior citizens.
explanation.definitionFit: Shampoo is the standard cleaning product for hair, a form of care for one's locks.

clue.text: Feed an excitement for assault drums

indicators.note: excitement means the letters are stirred up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Feeding a frenzied crowd leads to an attack on the drums.
explanation.definitionFit: To assault the eardrums with noise is to make someone unable to hear, a figurative paraphrase.

clue.text: See 5
Child who's up for concert

parts.note: being up means being in residence at university, in British usage
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A child who is awake is ready for a show.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a student is 'up' at university, so a child who's up is a uni son. 'Concert' is agreement, not a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in concert means acting together in agreement, the sense of in unison.

clue.text: Moderately content age

indicators.note: content means what is contained inside the word 'Moderately'

explanation.surface: Fairly satisfied with getting older.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a period of history, synonymous with an age.

clue.text: Outbreaks of bleak drizzle, each followed by showers and loss of brightness

indicators.note: each followed by means the showers come straight after both opening letters, so one copy goes between them
outbreaks are the starts of things, so the opening letters of 'bleak' and 'drizzle' are wanted

parts.note: showers of water are rain
the same showers come again after the second letter

explanation.surface: A weather forecast of grey drizzle and showers, with less sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'each followed by' puts RAIN after both B and D: one copy sits between them and one comes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A brain drain is the emigration of clever people, so a nation loses its brightest minds.

clue.text: See 5
Provocative starlet's pose — don't stare!

indicators.note: provocative means stirring things up, so the letters are rearranged once the others are gone

parts.note: used letter for letter, its S included

explanation.surface: A warning not to ogle a young actress posing bare-breasted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don't stare' removes the letters of STARE from STARLETSPOSE, leaving LTSPOSE, which 'Provocative' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A topless pose is the provocative one the clue pictures, so the whole clue serves as definition.

clue.text: Irish playwright born brave

parts.note: George Bernard Shaw was the Irish playwright
née means born, used for a maiden name

explanation.surface: An Irish dramatist was born courageous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brave' looks like an adjective; it is a noun for a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: A brave is a Native American warrior, and the Shawnee are a Native American people.

clue.text: Musicians' leader delayed by crowd trouble

indicators.note: the leading letter is held back and put at the end

parts.note: a trio is a group of three musicians

explanation.surface: A band's frontman was held up by a disturbance in the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A riot is a violent disturbance by a crowd, so crowd trouble paraphrases it.

clue.text: Businessman's faith initially is in American stockholder

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of 'faith'
in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a rancher keeps livestock, the stock of an American ranch

explanation.surface: A trader's belief is invested in a US shareholder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stockholder' suggests shares, but the stock here is cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A franchiser is a business that licenses others to trade under its name and system.
